claims.statement: For the fixed favorable-leaf selector F and k=p-1, the complete selected sum equals sum over v in F of q_v(k+1)-q_v(k), where q_v(j) counts independent j-sets of H_v meeting W_v; this is exactly the aggregate tagged-layer inequality, without itself proving its sign.
claims.scope: Every finite ordinary tree and p satisfying x(T)+2<=p and 3p<2alpha(T)+1, with the contract definitions of H_v, W_v, R_v and F.
claims.reason: retained: H_v-W_v=R_v, so q_v is the marked-layer count; subtracting the rank-k differences gives q_v(k+1)-q_v(k) rowwise. The fixed selector and distinct leaf tags are preserved. This is only an exact reformulation.

claims.statement: For a fixed eligible instance with the exact selected set F and the stated within-tag incidence graph, a feasible unit-demand, unit-capacity fractional matching from the tagged upper layer to the tagged lower layer is a sufficient certificate for the primary inequality; Hall deficiency obstructs this certificate but does not by itself refute the scalar aggregate.
claims.scope: One fixed finite eligible ordinary tree and p; no universal feasibility assertion. Nodes retain original-leaf tags and edges are within-tag set inclusions.
claims.reason: retained: summing flow constraints proves the layer cardinality inequality, and finite bipartite max-flow/min-cut gives Hall's condition for feasibility. The eligible T22 and T60 controls each have a selected positive row, so the certificate fails there despite negative full sums; this limits its usefulness without invalidating its conditional sufficiency.

claims.statement: C1-U3 provides no resolution of the universal lower-region aggregate: it proves neither universal tagged-flow feasibility nor a positive complete-sum ordinary-tree witness. Its particular unit-flow certificate is unavailable universally, as shown by eligible T22 and T60 Hall-deficient rows whose complete selected sums are negative.
claims.scope: Assessment of the C1-U3 route and its specific tagged unit-capacity transport method; no verdict on the primary target.
claims.reason: retained_narrowed: the route leaves the target open, and the standing controls sharpen the method limitation. For each control, one selected row has q_v(k+1)>q_v(k), producing a Hall-deficient whole-tag subset, while the exact complete aggregate is negative. A failed stronger certificate is not a target counterexample.

limitations: No proof or refutation of the primary lower-region aggregate is established.
The T22 and T60 controls were checked from their listed exact JSON fields; their tree coefficient vectors were not independently regenerated.
The matching failure rules out universal feasibility of this certificate, not the aggregate inequality or other proof methods.
No new finite computation or literature result is used.
